candidates.title: LIBRE: Lookahead I/O-Efficient Buffered REbatching for MoE Serving
candidates.venue: IEEE International Conference on Cluster Computing
candidates.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to scale, the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture has become a pivotal technology, offering enhanced model capacity with high computational efficiency. However, MoE faces a critical performance bottleneck during inference: because tokens dynamically select different experts, batching them often leads to excessive I/O overhead when expert selections diverge. This creates an I/O-bound environment that severely limits throughput scalability as batch sizes increase. We propose LIBRE, a Lookahead I/O-efficient Buffered RE-batching framework designed to mitigate redundant I/O by temporarily storing tokens and regrouping those that share the same expert. Central to LIBRE is a “Lookahead Scheduling” algorithm, which optimizes throughput by considering not only current token counts but also the interdependencies between Attention and MLP modules. By incorporating a decayed scoring mechanism based on token distributions already visible in subsequent layers, the proposed scheduler improves batch efficiency while mitigating token starvation. We evaluate LIBRE on a simulation platform modeling a wafer-scale AI chip equipped with a hardware reorder buffer (ROB). Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly enhances throughput across various datasets, achieving a 50% throughput improvement for Llama4 and up to 85% for Qwen3.
candidates.reason: MoEサービングで専門家選択の発散によるI/O過多に対し、同一専門家を選ぶトークンを先読みスケジューリングでバッファし再バッチ化するLIBREにより推論スループットを改善するMoE推論向け手法である。

candidates.title: Native Dual Pools or Shared Paging? Memory Organization for Concurrent Hybrid LLM Serving
candidates.abstract: Hybrid attention-SSM serving combines growing attention KV with fixed-size recurrent and convolution state whose allocation units, reuse boundaries, and lifetimes differ. We implement four memory organizations in a modified vLLM runtime: a coarse shared-page baseline (S0), checkpoint-internal recurrent paging (S1), paging with convolution-slot packing (S2), and native dual pools (D0). Nine evaluation questions cover storage costs and serving behavior. The cumulative S0-S1-S2 refinement improves completed-output throughput and tail completion time at the main operating point. D0-S2 performance varies with memory budget, offered load, and admission headroom. Shared-prefix workloads yield larger stepwise gains; gains also persist in a no-sharing control with equal recorded input-work totals. State traces identify recurrent-checkpoint availability as the limit on joint reuse in the tested S2 runs. Extending producer-side checkpoint lifetime increases reusable depth at a fixed page budget. A fresh-seed SHARE/ISOLATE comparison estimates a positive retention interaction, with a primary confidence interval that includes zero. Retained-state continuation correctness remains unresolved. These findings motivate evaluating physical state representation together with request admission and checkpoint lifetime when designing memory management for concurrent hybrid-model serving.
candidates.reason: 注意KVと固定長回帰・畳み込み状態が混在するハイブリッドLLMサービング向けに、改変vLLM上で共有ページングやネイティブ二重プール等の4種のメモリ組織を実装比較しスループットと尾部完了時間を評価したサービングメモリ研究である。
